bss.topic: Imigração europeia e o trabalho livre

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual foi o principal produto agrícola que atraiu imigrantes europeus para São Paulo no século XIX?
questions.hint: Pense nas grandes fazendas do Oeste Paulista.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Como se chama o trabalho em que a pessoa recebe pagamento e não é propriedade de ninguém, que substituiu aos poucos a escravidão?
questions.hint: É o contrário do trabalho escravizado.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Em que ano foi aprovada a Lei de Terras no Brasil?
questions.hint: Foi no mesmo ano da lei que proibiu o tráfico de africanos escravizados.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: O que a Lei de Terras de 1850 determinou?
options: As terras públicas só poderiam ser obtidas por compra
Todo imigrante ganharia um lote de graça
As terras seriam divididas entre os escravizados libertos
A Igreja passaria a controlar as terras
questions.answer: As terras públicas só poderiam ser obtidas por compra
questions.hint: Pense em quem tinha dinheiro para comprar terra.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Por que a Lei de Terras dificultou que imigrantes pobres e ex-escravizados se tornassem proprietários?
options: Porque eles não tinham dinheiro para comprar terras
Porque eles eram proibidos de trabalhar no campo
Porque só podiam morar nas cidades
Porque as terras eram todas da Coroa portuguesa
questions.answer: Porque eles não tinham dinheiro para comprar terras
questions.hint: A terra virou mercadoria.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual lei de 1850 proibiu o tráfico de africanos escravizados para o Brasil?
questions.hint: Tem o nome de um ministro da época.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Em que ano a Lei Áurea aboliu a escravidão no Brasil?
questions.hint: Foi um ano antes da Proclamação da República.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: No sistema de parceria, como o imigrante pagava a viagem e as despesas iniciais?
options: Ficava endividado com o fazendeiro e pagava com o trabalho
O governo pagava tudo e ele não devia nada
Ele já chegava com a viagem paga pela família
Trabalhava de graça só no primeiro mês
questions.answer: Ficava endividado com o fazendeiro e pagava com o trabalho
questions.hint: Pense em por que muitos parceiros se revoltaram.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Por que o sistema de parceria fracassou?
options: Os imigrantes ficavam presos a dívidas e havia conflitos com os fazendeiros
Os fazendeiros pagavam salários altos demais
O café deixou de ser vendido
Os imigrantes recusavam-se a plantar alimentos
questions.answer: Os imigrantes ficavam presos a dívidas e havia conflitos com os fazendeiros
questions.hint: Houve revoltas, como a da fazenda Ibicaba.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: De que países vinham principalmente os parceiros da revolta na fazenda Ibicaba, nos anos 1850?
questions.hint: Eram imigrantes da Europa central.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual sistema de trabalho substituiu a parceria nas fazendas de café, com pagamento fixo pelo cuidado dos cafeeiros e mais um valor pela colheita?
questions.hint: O trabalhador era chamado de colono.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual destes direitos o colono costumava ter no colonato?
options: Plantar alimentos para a família entre os pés de café
Ficar com metade da fazenda depois de 5 anos
Não trabalhar na época da colheita
questions.answer: Plantar alimentos para a família entre os pés de café
questions.hint: Isso ajudava a família a se alimentar.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual grupo de imigrantes europeus foi o mais numeroso nas fazendas de café paulistas no fim do século XIX?
questions.hint: Muitos vieram fugindo de crises no próprio país.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Por que o governo da província de São Paulo passou a pagar as passagens dos imigrantes a partir dos anos 1880?
options: Para garantir mão de obra para o café com o fim da escravidão próximo
questions.answer: Para garantir mão de obra para o café com o fim da escravidão próximo
questions.hint: Pense no que estava acontecendo com a escravidão nessa década.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Explique por que muitos ex-escravizados não foram contratados como trabalhadores livres nas fazendas após 1888 e quais foram as consequências disso.
questions.hint: Pense na preferência dos fazendeiros, no racismo e na falta de acesso à terra.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Compare o sistema de parceria e o colonato: o que mudou para o trabalhador imigrante?
questions.hint: Pense em dívidas, forma de pagamento e direito de plantar.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What is the key idea of the von Neumann architecture?
options: Instructions and data are stored in the same memory
Instructions and data are stored in separate memories
Programs are stored only on paper
questions.answer: Instructions and data are stored in the same memory
questions.hint: It is often called the 'stored program' concept.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which register holds the address of the next instruction to be fetched?
questions.hint: Its name says it keeps count through the program.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which register stores the results of calculations carried out by the ALU?
questions.hint: It accumulates results.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What does MAR stand for?
questions.hint: It holds an address, not data.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which register temporarily holds data or an instruction that has just been read from, or is about to be written to, memory?
questions.hint: Think 'data', not 'address'.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which register holds the instruction currently being decoded and executed?
questions.hint: The word 'current' is a clue.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which part of the CPU carries out arithmetic and logical operations?
questions.hint: Its name includes 'arithmetic'.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What is the main job of the Control Unit?
options: To decode instructions and coordinate the other components
To display output on the screen
questions.answer: To decode instructions and coordinate the other components
questions.hint: It sends control signals.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which bus carries memory addresses from the CPU to main memory?
questions.hint: The name tells you what it carries.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which bus is one-way (unidirectional)?
questions.hint: Only the CPU sends locations to memory.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Put the stages of the cycle in the correct order.
questions.hint: The CPU must get the instruction before understanding it.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: During the fetch stage, what happens straight after the address in the PC is copied to the MAR?
questions.hint: The PC must get ready for the next instruction.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: A program counter currently holds the value 104. Instructions are fetched one after another with no jumps. What value will the PC hold after three more instructions have been fetched?
questions.hint: Each fetch adds 1.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What is meant by the 'von Neumann bottleneck'?
options: Instructions and data share one bus, which limits speed
The CPU has too many registers
The screen is slower than the keyboard
questions.answer: Instructions and data share one bus, which limits speed
questions.hint: Think about traffic on a single road.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Describe what happens to the PC, MAR, MDR and CIR during the fetch stage of the fetch–decode–execute cycle.
questions.hint: Follow the address from the PC to memory and the instruction back to the CIR.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage of storing both instructions and data in the same memory.
questions.hint: Think about flexibility versus the shared pathway.

en.topic: Reading non-fiction: explicit and implicit information

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What is explicit information in a text?
options: Information you have to work out from clues
questions.hint: 'Explicit' means clearly expressed.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What is implicit information?
options: Information suggested but not stated directly
A list of facts at the end of a text
questions.answer: Information suggested but not stated directly
questions.hint: You need to read between the lines.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which word means to find and take information directly from a text?
questions.hint: It begins with 're-'.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which word means to work out a meaning from clues in a text?
questions.hint: It is the skill of 'reading between the lines'.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which of these is a non-fiction text?
options: A newspaper report about a flood
A fairy tale about a dragon
A poem about an imaginary island
A short story about a talking cat
questions.answer: A newspaper report about a flood
questions.hint: Non-fiction is about real events and facts.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Read: 'The museum opens at 9 a.m. and closes at 5 p.m. on weekdays.' What time does the museum close on weekdays?
questions.hint: This is stated directly.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Read: 'After the storm, the town hall's roof lay in the car park.' What can you infer?
options: The town hall was being repaired
questions.hint: Think about what force would be needed.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Read: 'By the third hour of the hike, Maya's water bottle was empty and her steps were getting slower.' What can you infer about Maya?
options: She was becoming tired and thirsty
She was enjoying a quick walk
She had brought too much water
questions.answer: She was becoming tired and thirsty
questions.hint: Look at both clues together.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Read: 'Tickets sold out within ten minutes of going on sale.' What does this imply about the event?
questions.hint: Think about why tickets would go so quickly.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Read: 'The volunteers worked through the night, refusing to stop until every sandbag was in place.' Which quality does this imply the volunteers had?
questions.hint: Look at the phrase 'refusing to stop'.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which statement is explicit information from this sentence: 'The bridge, built in 1902, carries over 40,000 vehicles a day'?
questions.hint: Choose what is actually written.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Read: 'Despite the rain, the queue for the new café stretched round the block.' What can you infer?
options: People were very keen to try the café
The café was very small inside
questions.answer: People were very keen to try the café
questions.hint: Why would people wait in the rain?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Read: 'The old factory's windows were boarded up and weeds pushed through the cracked tarmac.' What can you infer about the factory?
options: It has been abandoned for some time
questions.answer: It has been abandoned for some time
questions.hint: Weeds take time to grow.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: When you make an inference in an exam answer, what should you always include?
options: Evidence from the text to support it
A summary of the whole text
Your favourite quotation from another book
A list of the writer's techniques only
questions.answer: Evidence from the text to support it
questions.hint: Show how you know.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Read: 'Every morning, Mr Hale's dog waits by the gate at exactly 7.45, its tail already wagging before the school bus appears.' What can you infer about the dog's routine? Support your answer with evidence.
questions.hint: Use the time and the dog's behaviour as clues.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Read: 'The charity's shelves, once full, now held only a few tins of beans and a single packet of pasta.' What does this suggest about the charity's situation, and how do you know?
questions.hint: Compare 'once full' with 'now'.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What does 'evaluate' mean in a reading question?
options: Judge how effective or convincing something is
questions.answer: Judge how effective or convincing something is
questions.hint: It involves making a judgement.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: A 'to what extent' question asks you to:
options: Decide how far you agree, weighing different sides
questions.answer: Decide how far you agree, weighing different sides
questions.hint: Your answer can be 'partly'.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What is the word for a reasoned decision you reach after considering evidence?
questions.hint: It is what a judge makes.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which phrase best shows a balanced evaluation?
options: To some extent I agree, because…, however…
This is the best text ever written.
questions.answer: To some extent I agree, because…, however…
questions.hint: Look for both sides.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What is the best evidence to support a point about a text?
options: A short, relevant quotation from the text
A long copy of the whole paragraph
A guess about the writer's life
questions.answer: A short, relevant quotation from the text
questions.hint: Precise and relevant is best.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: A student wants to argue against the statement. What should they do?
options: Find evidence that challenges it and explain why
Repeat the statement in capital letters
questions.answer: Find evidence that challenges it and explain why
questions.hint: Counter-evidence needs explaining too.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Statement: 'The writer presents the city as a frightening place.' Which quotation best SUPPORTS this?
options: 'Shadows crept along the alleys like hungry animals.'
questions.answer: 'Shadows crept along the alleys like hungry animals.'
questions.hint: Which image creates fear?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Statement: 'The writer presents the city as a frightening place.' Which quotation best CHALLENGES this?
questions.hint: Look for a positive image.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which word shows that a reader is making a tentative (not certain) judgement?
questions.hint: It suggests possibility.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which sentence is the best start to a critical evaluation?
options: I largely agree with this statement because the writer's imagery repeatedly creates tension.
This text is about a city.
questions.answer: I largely agree with this statement because the writer's imagery repeatedly creates tension.
questions.hint: It gives a clear judgement and a reason.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What does 'critical' mean in 'critical reading'?
options: Thinking carefully and questioning what you read
questions.answer: Thinking carefully and questioning what you read
questions.hint: It is not the same as complaining.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: In an evaluation, why is it useful to comment on the effect of a word on the reader?
options: It explains how the evidence supports your judgement
It shows you know the writer's age
questions.answer: It explains how the evidence supports your judgement
questions.hint: Evidence needs explanation.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which connective is best for introducing a counter-argument?
questions.hint: It signals a contrast.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which is the most effective conclusion to a 'to what extent' answer?
options: A clear final judgement that sums up how far you agree and why
A new quotation not discussed before
A list of all the paragraphs
questions.answer: A clear final judgement that sums up how far you agree and why
questions.hint: End with your overall decision.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Statement: 'Reading books is more valuable than watching films.' To what extent do you agree? Give one reason for and one against, then your judgement.
questions.hint: Weigh both sides before deciding.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: A student wrote: 'The writer makes the storm seem exciting.' Suggest one piece of evidence a writer might use to support this and explain its effect.
questions.hint: Think of a vivid verb or image linked to energy.
